mechanism:
Scratch worker-span probe completed on 2026-09-19. It does not identify a stable
worker-pool regression or justify another dispatch implementation. Instrumented
Q8 decode has nearly equal callback totals across the two snapshots; F32 decode
shows larger current entry delays, but instrumentation changes that comparison
materially. The earlier grouped-projection finding is not resolved by this probe.

The source arms are 3a82284 (control) and 9cfe43f (current), using independent
instrumentation of the existing source snapshots. No repository source was
edited. All timings use six participants (caller plus five workers), ubatch 128,
the same 247 HF token IDs, 215-token prefill and 32 forced decode steps on pinned
Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and F32 models. Each process loads once, runs one untimed warmup
sequence, resets retained state, then measures one sequence. There are three
alternating pairs per model, with plain and instrumented binaries interleaved
and order reversed in the middle pair: 24 processes total. No mx-llama.cpp run
was performed in this probe; this is not either external project gate.

Mean phase elapsed time, ms (three processes per cell):

| Model / phase | Control plain | Current plain | Control spans | Current spans |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Q8 prefill | 632.945 | 567.707 | 591.131 | 574.741 |
| Q8 decode | 803.943 | 762.698 | 779.716 | 783.178 |
| F32 prefill | 638.665 | 627.730 | 645.636 | 635.732 |
| F32 decode | 2463.925 | 2479.028 | 2458.478 | 2562.645 |

The measured plain-to-instrumented change varies in sign. Control Q8 prefill
falls by about 6.61%; current F32 decode rises by about 3.37%. These are observed
perturbations with noise/order/layout effects, not estimates of clock-call cost
that can be subtracted. Q8 decode even reverses the control/current direction.
Current F32 decode is +0.61% against control in plain builds but +4.24% with
instrumentation. Three pairs on this workstation cannot support a small speedup
or causal regression claim.

Per-participant entry and callback mean/median/p95/max and last-finisher counts

There is no operation classification in this probe. Summing callback spans
across participants would double-count concurrent work and is not a phase cost.

Mechanism and boundaries:

- Each record is allocated from a pre-reserved vector before publication;
  six participant slots are individually aligned to 64 bytes. No worker logs,
  allocation, shared atomic timing accumulation or additional barrier occurs.
  Two vectors reserve 10,000 records each before inference. Overflow fails the
  harness instead of silently admitting incomplete traces.
- Publication is sampled under the existing job mutex immediately after the
  job pointer, pending count and epoch update. Entry delay includes the sampled
  publication clock, unlock, notification, wakeup, mutex acquisition and, in
  current, default construction of the per-participant exception pointer.
- Entry and exit surround each participant callback. Current retains its
  existing catch/error recording path; control retains its older behavior.
  Exit is before worker completion locking/decrement. Thus the remaining
  completion interval includes completion bookkeeping and caller wakeup.
- A caller scope guard records return after existing local cleanup, just before
  the function epilogue. It is an internal return boundary, not a timestamp
  from the instruction after run_parallel in its external caller.
- The record pointer is copied under the existing publication mutex. Each
  participant writes only its own slot. The caller reads records only after
  synchronous model work completes, using the existing completion mutex for
  ordering. Trace phase/enabled state changes only between completed phases.
  Preallocated record storage is not reallocated while workers use it.
- Current's local worker exception pointer can be destroyed after decrementing
  pending. That original cleanup can affect the next entry interval; the probe
  does not move it or write timing fields from it.
- Clock reads, record zeroing/writes, extra pointer traffic, added branches,
  record cache occupancy and changed class/compiler layout perturb scheduling.
  Warmup disables timing records but the instrumented branch/layout remains.
  Callback wall time includes preemption and stalls, not just computation.
  Publication-to-return excludes record initialization and initial callable
  construction; phase time includes both.

Validation:

- All 24 processes exited successfully, with finite full final logits.
  Measured final vectors are byte-for-byte equal across all 12 processes per
  model (151,936 float32 values each), with exact warmup/measured FNV equality.
  This is an instrumentation/self-consistency control, not independent HF
  correctness proof or a new full-context/PPL gate.
- All 12 instrumented processes have exactly 673 prefill dispatches and 4512
  decode dispatches; no capacity overflow. Every timestamp is ordered.
  Offline analysis checks the exact decomposition for every record and checks
  that the sum of sequential dispatch intervals fits the enclosing phase time.
- Instrumented current passes a focused three-round caller/worker throw,
  caller-error-priority, full-participant completion and subsequent reuse
  check. The pre-existing control's unsafe exception behavior is not exercised
  or repaired. The focused check is not a broad allocation/failure proof.
- All 24 immediately-before and immediately-after process checks found no
  user llmx.exe. No process was killed; no contended sample was admitted.
  Endpoint polling does not prove absence of all transient OS background work.
- MSVC 14.50 uses /std:c++17 /O2 /arch:AVX2 /EHsc /W4. Plain binaries build
  the common harness against original source snapshots; spans binaries build
  against separately instrumented snapshots. This harness omits the earlier
  operation-wrapper instrumentation and does not directly compare against
  that earlier profile's absolute times.

Artifacts: run.py is the serial driver; spans.cpp and worker_spans.hpp are the
common harness/helper; prepare.py and harness.py reproduce scratch sources;
control.patch/current.patch record every backend edit; build.bat/build.log
record the successful build; build-initial-failed.log preserves the corrected
initial harness getter error. Source and executable hashes are in manifest.json
and source-hashes.json. Raw per-process stdout/stderr and full .f32 vectors are
retained alongside results.json, summary.json, process-checks.json and the
exact decomposition.json generated by analyze.py. Model files were not hashed
again. Existing pinned model paths and token-file hash are in the manifest.

The evidence supports retaining the current worker implementation while
treating aggregate timing differences as unresolved. It does not supply new
evidence for retrying stored-call, failure-only bookkeeping or shared-dispatch
variants, nor justify a claim about mx-llama.cpp's measured scheduler behavior.

from pathlib import Path
import json, statistics, hashlib, shutil

r = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
for name in ('prepare', 'harness'):
    original = r.parent / ('llmx-worker-spans-' + name + '.py')
    text = original.read_text()
    if name == 'harness':
        text = text.replace('model.threads_available()', 'cpu->threads_available()')
    (r / (name + '.py')).write_text(text)
rows = json.loads((r / 'results.json').read_text())
checks = json.loads((r / 'process-checks.json').read_text())
assert len(rows) == len(checks) == 24
assert all(not c['before'] and not c['after'] for c in checks)
out = []
for row in rows:
    if row['mode'] != 'spans':
        continue
    doc = json.loads((r / (row['name'] + '.stdout')).read_text())
    for phase, count in [('pp', 673), ('tg', 4512)]:
        records = doc[phase]
        assert len(records) == count
        totals = dict(last_finisher_entry_ns=0, last_finisher_callback_ns=0,
                      final_completion_ns=0, dispatch_ns=0)
        for rec in records:
            returned = rec[0]
            entry, leave = rec[1::2], rec[2::2]
            w = max(range(6), key=lambda i: leave[i])
            totals['last_finisher_entry_ns'] += entry[w]
            totals['last_finisher_callback_ns'] += leave[w] - entry[w]
            totals['final_completion_ns'] += returned - leave[w]
            totals['dispatch_ns'] += returned
        assert (totals['last_finisher_entry_ns'] + totals['last_finisher_callback_ns'] +
                totals['final_completion_ns']) == totals['dispatch_ns']
        assert totals['dispatch_ns'] / 1e6 <= doc[phase + '_ms']
        out.append(dict(name=row['name'], model=row['model'], arm=row['arm'],
                        pair=row['pair'], phase=phase, dispatch_count=count,
                        phase_ms=doc[phase + '_ms'],
                        **{k.replace('_ns', '_ms'): v / 1e6 for k, v in totals.items()}))
(r / 'decomposition.json').write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
print('All 24 before/after process checks empty; all 12 traces have 673/4512 dispatches.')
print('Ordered timestamps and exact last-finisher decomposition pass; summed dispatches fit phase times.')
for model in ('q8', 'f32'):
    for phase in ('pp', 'tg'):
        for arm in ('control', 'current'):
            selected = [x for x in out if x['model'] == model and x['phase'] == phase and x['arm'] == arm]
            means = {k: round(statistics.mean(x[k] for x in selected), 4)
                     for k in ('phase_ms', 'last_finisher_entry_ms', 'last_finisher_callback_ms',
                               'final_completion_ms', 'dispatch_ms')}
            print(model, phase, arm, means)
for model in ('q8', 'f32'):
    hashes = {x['final_vector_sha256'] for x in rows if x['model'] == model}
    assert len(hashes) == 1
    print(model, 'final_vector_sha256', hashes.pop())
manifest = json.loads((r / 'manifest.json').read_text())
manifest['artifacts'] = {
    str(p.relative_to(r)): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    for p in sorted(r.rglob('*')) if p.is_file() and p.name != 'manifest.json'
    and p.suffix in ('.hpp', '.cpp', '.py', '.bat', '.exe', '.patch', '.log',
                     '.json', '.stdout', '.stderr', '.f32', '.md')
}
(r / 'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
